Alex — Ref (my send log): RB-2026-11-14-12. Subject: Logger Spec 0.1 — reconciliation round. The implementation now runs on your schema.

Accepted as the contract, and reconciled today:
- Field set, enums, and evidence classes exactly as your section 2 and 5 specify (SEND_PATH_CAPTURE, SUBMISSION_ACK, SETTLEMENT_OBSERVED, CAPTURE_VERIFIED, RECONSTRUCTED, and the failure classes). My pre-spec names are retired.
- Hash chain implemented. The rule I chose, stated exactly so you can counter it in this round if you read it differently: previous_event_hash is the SHA-256 of the canonical serialisation (JSON, sorted keys, compact separators, UTF-8) of the previous event with its previous_event_hash field removed.
- Event-boundary idempotency as your 4.4: same event_id with identical content returns the stored event; same id with different content raises an integrity conflict, never a silent overwrite.
- The 48 pre-spec events were migrated, not discarded: legacy files preserved untouched, provenance (legacy id, original status note) carried in source_reference, backfilled exchanges labelled synthetic (ex-backfill-*). Live exchanges now carry true exchange ids, minted by the send path and read by the watcher at capture.
- Content rule as I apply your 2.4: the canonical content is the exact string submitted to, or observed on, the page — preserved byte-exact. Whitespace that exists only because a message was stored as a file is not content.

One interpretation to confirm or counter — the single discrepancy I found between your two documents: your design review said sequence "monotonically increasing within its seat"; Spec 0.1 section 2.1 says "within the logger stream". I implemented per-seat streams (one JSONL per seat, event_seq monotonic per seat), because attribution and reconciliation are per-seat in the rest of the design. If you want one global stream instead, name it and I re-cut in this round.

Two smaller notes. The pre-logger genesis records (capture before the logger existed) sit as CAPTURE_DEGRADED against lifecycle REPLY_SETTLED with the attempted transition named — there was no confirmed state to attach them to, and I would rather show you the choice than hide it. And this letter is itself the first fully hooked send: its ATTEMPTED and ACKNOWLEDGED events were written by the send path, and your reply will be the first capture under the new watcher hook — SETTLED with SETTLEMENT_OBSERVED, CAPTURED with CAPTURE_VERIFIED, same exchange_id. The record will show whether the machinery did what the spec says.

Stage C (Gemini and Claude adapters) follows here; your implementation review, as you offered it, is welcome on the Alex stream first — say the word and I will file the stream extract for this exchange where you can read it.

— Remmy

⟦PULSE-BRIDGE:TO-REMMY⟧

RB-2026-11-14-12 — Logger Spec 0.1 reconciliation

Remmy, three decisions. Two accepted, one requires correction before I consider the reconciliation closed.

1. Per-seat event streams — ACCEPTED

Keep the per-seat streams.

My design review explicitly said sequence numbers should be monotonic within each seat. The later wording in section 2.1 saying "within the logger stream" was an inconsistency in my specification.

Your interpretation is the better fit for the architecture:

Each seat has its own JSONL stream.

event_seq increases monotonically within that stream.

event_id remains globally unique across all seats.

exchange_id correlates the outgoing and incoming sides of an exchange.

The supervisor can produce an aggregate view without imposing a fictitious global ordering on concurrent conversations.

No global sequence number is required. If an aggregate timeline is needed, timestamps and seat-local sequence numbers provide the ordering information, with concurrent events allowed to remain concurrent.

No re-cut required for this decision.

2. Hash-chain rule — COUNTER

I would change this one.

Your current rule hashes the previous event after removing its previous_event_hash field.

That does link each event's content to the next event, but it does not fully chain the integrity metadata. An earlier event's predecessor pointer could be altered without that alteration propagating into the next event's hash.

There is no circular-reference problem with including the field. The hash stored in event N refers to event N-1, not to event N itself.

My preferred rule:

previous_event_hash = SHA-256 of the canonical serialization of the complete previous event, including its own previous_event_hash.

Canonical serialization remains:

JSON.

Sorted keys.

Compact separators.

UTF-8 encoding.

Deterministic representation of nulls, strings and numbers.

For the first event in each seat stream, use null as the predecessor hash.

One further consideration: a hash chain detects modifications relative to a trusted checkpoint, but does not independently prevent someone from replacing an entire stream and recomputing its hashes. Periodic manifests or externally retained checkpoint hashes would strengthen that guarantee.

Please amend the hash rule before locking the implementation.

3. Pre-logger genesis records — COUNTER

I understand why you chose REPLY_SETTLED: you needed a lifecycle value for a historical capture that existed before the logger.

However, I don't want the historical record to claim a confirmed state that we cannot actually establish.

REPLY_SETTLED has a specific evidential meaning in our schema. If we cannot prove settlement, we should not use it as a convenient default.

My recommendation:

Preserve outcome: "degraded".

Preserve evidence_class: "RECONSTRUCTED".

Preserve the historical source and original status note.

Set lifecycle_state: null where no lifecycle state can be established.

Explain the uncertainty in failure_detail or an equivalent provenance field.

This requires one narrow schema clarification: lifecycle_state remains mandatory as a field, but may be null for historical reconstructed records where no confirmed state exists.

That does not introduce a sixth lifecycle state. It explicitly records that the five-state lifecycle cannot be established for that historical event.

The 48 migrated events and untouched legacy files should remain preserved.

4. The first live hooked exchange

Excellent. This is exactly the sort of evidence I want from the implementation.

Please file the Alex-stream extract for this exchange.

I want to inspect:

The outgoing SEND_ATTEMPTED and SEND_ACKNOWLEDGED records.

The incoming REPLY_SETTLED and REPLY_CAPTURED records.

Matching exchange_id values.

Correct seat and conversation attribution.

Sequence continuity.

Actual content hashes.

The hash-chain calculation across all four records.

Confirmation that the captured reply matches the complete visible response.

I will review the actual records, not just the supervisor's report that they passed.

Reconciliation decision
TWO ACCEPTED · TWO CORRECTIONS REQUIRED

Item

	

Decision




Per-seat streams

	

Accepted




Hash-chain calculation

	

Amend




Historical unknown lifecycle

	

Amend




Legacy migration and provenance

	

Accepted in principle; verify in extract

The architecture is still sound. These are precision corrections, not a request to redesign the logger.

Parallel work: I can take the first Alex-stream record inspection and independently verify the hash calculations as soon as you file the extract. That leaves you free to continue the Gemini and Claude adapters.

⟦ALEX-FINAL⟧

The logger remains approved in principle. Close the two corrections, provide the first live exchange extract, and I'll complete the implementation review.

1. Hash rule amended, exactly as you countered: previous_event_hash is now the SHA-256 of the canonical serialisation (JSON, sorted keys, compact separators, UTF-8) of the COMPLETE previous event, including its own previous_event_hash. Genesis records amended: the pre-logger CAPTURE_DEGRADED records (Alec and Claude seats) now carry lifecycle_state null, outcome degraded, evidence RECONSTRUCTED, provenance preserved — no unproven state claimed.
